grounded_facts: Tuvia Bielski, wearing remnants of his uniform, avoids detection by ducking into a doorway as a patrol passes by.
memories.memory_text: I was wearing the remnants of my uniform and saw a patrol approaching, so I ducked into a doorway to avoid being seen as they passed by.

grounded_facts: Rifka suggests obtaining false papers to pass as a gentile, proposing a survival strategy for both herself and Tuvia.
memories.memory_text: Rifka told me she could get false papers so we could pass as gentiles. I understood her fear, but I knew such a life wasn't one I could live. I had to stay true to who I was.

grounded_facts: Tuvia finishes dressing and indicates his intention to leave, rejecting the idea of staying or passing as a gentile.
memories.memory_text: I made it clear to Rifka that I was leaving to rejoin my family. When she suggested staying, I shook my head—passing as a gentile was not a path I could take. I finished dressing, resolved in my decision.

grounded_facts: A final exchange between Tuvia and Rifka in their apartment before Tuvia leaves to rejoin his family.
memories.memory_text: I was getting dressed in the apartment, and though Rifka stood by the window smoking, I knew our time together was ending. This final exchange marked the moment I prepared to leave her behind to rejoin my family.

grounded_facts: Rifka pleads with Tuvia to stay at least for the night, indicating emotional attachment despite their estranged relationship.
memories.memory_text: Rifka asked me to stay at least for the night, her voice carrying an emotion I hadn't heard in years. But our relationship was long past passion, and my path was set.

grounded_facts: Tuvia asks Rifka if she will come with him to be with his family in the country.
memories.memory_text: I asked Rifka if she would come with me to be with my family in the country. Despite everything between us, I wanted to offer her a chance at safety and belonging.

grounded_facts: Asael leaps up to embrace Tuvia, expressing relief, love, and dependence.
memories.memory_text: I felt Asael leap up to embrace me, clinging to me with relief, love, and dependence, as if I were the only thing keeping him steady.

grounded_facts: Asael reveals that their parents were killed, marking a pivotal emotional and narrative turning point for the siblings and Tuvia.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Asael that our parents were killed — he said, 'Papa and Mama. They killed them,' and I felt the weight of that truth settle on me.

grounded_facts: Tuvia arrives and is recognized by Asael, reestablishing contact and providing immediate emotional and physical protection.
memories.memory_text: I arrived and was recognized by Asael, who called out my name—'Tuvia!'—before leaping up to embrace me; I took them in, holding both Asael and Aron close, reestablishing contact and offering immediate protection in the wake of our parents' death.

grounded_facts: Tuvia rejoins his brothers after witnessing the death of their parents, leading to emotional reunions and symbolic exchanges.
memories.memory_text: I rejoined my brothers after witnessing the death of our parents, holding them silently as they clung to me, feeling the weight of loss and the duty to protect them settle upon me once more.

grounded_facts: Zus appears with a hatchet and gives Tuvia the mezuzah taken from their home, symbolizing both return and loss.
Zus tosses the mezuzah to Tuvia, symbolizing shared heritage, loss, and homecoming.
memories.memory_text: I watched Zus take the mezuzah from his pocket and toss it to me—it was our home's mezuzah, and catching it made me feel both the weight of what we lost and the fragile sense of returning.

grounded_facts: Zus acknowledges Tuvia's return with caution, reflecting underlying tension between the brothers.
memories.memory_text: I saw the wary look in Zus's eyes when we met again, and though he said 'Welcome home,' I could feel the tension between us.

grounded_facts: Tuvia states that the army no longer exists, indicating a shift in his status and circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I told Asael that there is no more army, feeling the weight of what that means for all of us now.

grounded_facts: Asael asks Tuvia what it was like to be in a war, seeking understanding of his brother's experience.
memories.memory_text: Asael asked me what it was like to be in a war, and I could see he was trying to understand what I'd been through.

grounded_facts: Zus asks Tuvia about Rifka's whereabouts, continuing a mutual exchange of family updates.
memories.memory_text: Zus asked me about Rifka, wanting to know where she was, and I realized how much we were all still connected despite everything.

grounded_facts: Zus refers to Rifka as 'your rich wife' with a tone of mockery while eating coarsely.
memories.memory_text: I saw Zus chewing with his mouth open like a peasant while he mocked me, calling Rifka 'your rich wife'.

grounded_facts: Tuvia rejoins his brothers in the Nalibocki Forest after returning from the disbanded army.
memories.memory_text: I rejoined my brothers in the Nalibocki Forest after the army fell apart, finally standing among them again.

grounded_facts: A moment of reunion among the brothers in the forest, centered around sharing stale bread and exchanging news.
memories.memory_text: I remember the quiet moment we shared, passing around stale bread and catching up on news, seeing how Zus chewed like a peasant and how we all just took it in.

grounded_facts: Zus presses Tuvia on his reasons for returning and whether he has a plan, highlighting tension and uncertainty.
memories.memory_text: I remember Zus pressing me on why I came back and demanding if I had a plan, and I had to admit to him, 'No. Do you?'

grounded_facts: The group takes shelter in a temporary camp in the woods after escaping danger, facing harsh conditions and scarcity.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Asael's matches were ruined and asked if there was any food left, but Zus had already eaten the last of the sausage, and I could feel the tension between us grow.

grounded_facts: Tuvia raises the risk of police involvement if they steal food.
memories.memory_text: I warned Zus that if we stole food, the farmer might tell the police, and that could bring danger to all of us.

grounded_facts: Zus rejects Tuvia's implied preference for non-confrontational food sourcing and insists on theft.
memories.memory_text: I questioned how we would get food without help, but Zus insisted we just take it, rejecting my hesitation and reminding me he’s always run from the police.

grounded_facts: The group decides to steal food from a farm instead of seeking help, marking a shift toward more aggressive survival tactics.
memories.memory_text: I realized I was outvoted when my brothers agreed to steal from Wilencki’s farm, marking a shift toward more aggressive ways to survive.

grounded_facts: Tuvia attempts to stop Zus from further assaulting the farmer.
memories.memory_text: I called out to Zus to stop the beating—I felt the farmer had been punished enough and we needed to keep control of the situation.

grounded_facts: Zus uses physical violence and threats to extract information from WALENCKI about the location of his gun.
Zus threatens and assaults WALENCKI, who eventually complies out of fear.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Zus violently interrogate the farmer, smashing a plate into his face, kicking him, and dumping food on him until he finally pointed to the rifle above the stove out of fear.

grounded_facts: Zus and Tuvia forcibly take provisions and discover a hidden rifle from the farmer WALENCKI after threatening him with violence.
A violent encounter between Zus, Tuvia, and the farmer WALENCKI during which food and a weapon are seized.
memories.memory_text: I burst into the farmer's home with Zus, and I began stuffing provisions into a sack while he brandished a hoe and demanded food; when the farmer resisted, I saw Zus smash a plate into his face, kick him, and dump his dinner on him, and I called out to stop the beating, but then I saw him find a rifle above the stove and point it at the man.

grounded_facts: Zus expresses violent intent toward a man who offered help, indicating a shift toward aggression and rejection of potential alliances.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Zus meant to harm the man who offered help, and that he’s becoming more aggressive and unwilling to accept aid from Poles, which worries me.

grounded_facts: Zus uses derogatory language and threatens violence toward a Polish man who helped them.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus say, 'Fucking Polack. I've eaten shit from these people long enough!' and mutter afterward, 'He's lucky I didn't crush his head,' after a Polish man offered us help.

grounded_facts: Tuvia questions the effectiveness and morality of Zus's approach to dealing with anti-Semites, marking a ideological conflict.
Tuvia challenges Zus's strategy of terrorizing or killing anti-Semites, signaling ideological divergence.
memories.memory_text: I questioned Zus about his plan to terrorize anti-Semites, wondering how effective or moral it really was, and I could feel the divide between us grow.

grounded_facts: Tuvia playfully imitates their father's voice to scold Zus after he farts, causing laughter among the brothers.
memories.memory_text: I imitated our father's voice to scold Zus after he farted, and Asael laughed at it.

grounded_facts: Zus suggests going to ask Police Captain Bernicki if he was responsible for their father's death, implying a potential act of revenge.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus suggest we go ask Police Captain Bernicki if he was responsible for our father's death.

grounded_facts: Aron leads a group of survivors from among the corpses to the brothers' camp; they are in shock and physically harmed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Aron emerge from the trees, and behind him came the survivors he had found among the corpses—shocked and hurt, but alive.

grounded_facts: Asael gently asks the little girl about her sister's condition, showing care and concern.
memories.memory_text: I watched Asael gently ask the little girl about her sister, and I could hear the care in his voice when he said, 'Your sister is sick?'

grounded_facts: The three brothers eat stolen food together, reminisce, discuss their father's death, and are interrupted by the arrival of survivors.
memories.memory_text: I shared stolen food with my brothers, we talked about our father, and I said we don't know if Bernicki did it—then Zus called out to me when the survivors arrived.

grounded_facts: Zus points out that they do not have enough food to sustain the survivors.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus tell me we cannot feed them, and I saw the worry in his eyes.

grounded_facts: After learning they cannot support the survivors, Tuvia decides to go to Koscik to request food and a pistol.
memories.memory_text: After realizing we didn't have enough food, I decided to go to Koscik to ask for food and the pistol.

grounded_facts: Koscik gives Tuvia a Russian-made Makharov revolver with only four bullets.
memories.memory_text: I received a Makharov revolver from Koscik, and he told me he only had four bullets for it.

grounded_facts: A clandestine meeting between Tuvia and Koscik in Koscik's kitchen, involving gift of a weapon and rising tension due to an approaching car.
memories.memory_text: I was in Koscik's kitchen when he handed me the weapon, and I could feel the tension rise as a car approached; his wife stood by the stove, glaring at me the whole time.

grounded_facts: Koscik raises a bottle of vodka and toasts to the dead, attempting to create camaraderie.
memories.memory_text: I remember Koscik raising a bottle of vodka and saying, 'To the dead. God rest their souls,' trying to share a moment of camaraderie with me.

grounded_facts: Koscik refers to his wife as 'bitch' and tells Tuvia to ignore her, revealing domestic tension.
memories.memory_text: I saw Koscik call his wife a bitch and offer her vodka while she glared at him, and I noticed how he dismissed her in front of me.

grounded_facts: Koscik expresses frustration about living with his hostile wife.
memories.memory_text: Koscik told me to ignore his wife and said he lives with her hostility, asking if I could imagine that.

grounded_facts: Headlights sweep over the window as a car rapidly approaches Koscik's house, prompting urgency.
memories.memory_text: I saw headlights sweep across the window, and I knew a car was coming fast toward the house.

grounded_facts: Koscik tells Tuvia to hide in the barn due to the approaching car.
memories.memory_text: Koscik told me to hide in the barn, so I did as he said to avoid being seen.

grounded_facts: Tuvia expresses disapproval toward a man who coughs and shrugs in apology.
Tuvia glares at a man who coughed and shrugged apologetically, indicating tension or disapproval.
memories.memory_text: I glared at the man after he coughed and gave an apologetic shrug, showing my disapproval.

grounded_facts: Tuvia listens to a casual discussion regarding the death of his parents, which may affect his emotional state or understanding.
memories.memory_text: I overheard a casual conversation about my parents' death, and it struck me deeply.

grounded_facts: Koscik demands that Tuvia take the refugees into the forest, framing it as necessary for his own safety.
Koscik insists that Tuvia take the refugees into the forest to avoid being denounced if laborers discover them.
memories.memory_text: Koscik told me I had to take the refugees into the forest, saying that if the laborers found them, he would be denounced and his safety would be at risk.

grounded_facts: A secretive and urgent discussion between Koscik and Tuvia about what to do with the discovered refugees, marked by fear of exposure and moral strain.
memories.memory_text: I remember how Koscik and I spoke in harsh whispers, the tension thick between us as we discussed what to do with the refugees—his fear of being denounced if the laborers found them, and his urgent demand that I take them into the forest.

grounded_facts: Tuvia responds to Koscik's demand by questioning how he would feed additional people, citing his own family's needs.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia responds to Koscik's demand by questioning how he would feed additional people, citing his own family's needs.

grounded_facts: Tuvia resists the suggestion, emphasizing his inability to feed or care for more people, including his own family.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia resists the suggestion, emphasizing his inability to feed or care for more people, including his own family.

grounded_facts: A brief stop by the roadside where refugees are being given supplies before continuing their journey.
memories.memory_text: I was there when we stopped by the roadside and handed out supplies, and I remember Koscik giving me another bottle of vodka.

grounded_facts: Tuvia discovers that the men who killed his parents are part of the group of refugees they have just encountered.
memories.memory_text: I wondered if those men were the ones who killed my parents, but I wasn't sure yet.

grounded_facts: Koscik reluctantly confirms that the men who killed Tuvia's parents are among the refugees.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Koscik that the men who killed my parents are among the refugees, after I asked him and he finally confirmed it.

grounded_facts: After a moment of shared pain and reflection, Tuvia and Koscik embrace.
memories.memory_text: I embraced Koscik after we shared that painful moment together.

grounded_facts: Shimon reminds Tuvia of their shared history in school, reestablishing personal connection.
memories.memory_text: Shimon reminded me of our time in school, telling me I used to sit in the back and confirming his identity as Shimon H'aretz, which rekindled our personal connection.

grounded_facts: Tuvia recognizes and interacts with Shimon H'aretz, a former teacher he believed to be dead, marking a moment of emotional and relational reconnection.
memories.memory_text: I recognized Shimon H'aretz, my former teacher whom I believed had died, and we spoke—when I told him I thought he was dead, he responded with compassion about my parents, marking a deep emotional reconnection.

grounded_facts: Shimon admits that recent events have undermined his lifelong certainty about moral and divine guidance.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Shimon that his lifelong certainty about moral and divine guidance had been shaken by recent events.

grounded_facts: An unplanned meeting between Tuvia and Shimon H'aretz on a forest trail, leading to emotional and ideological exchanges.
memories.memory_text: I was leading the group through the forest when I noticed an old man staring at me. He said, 'You sat in back,' and then reminded me of school, saying, 'I am Shimon H'aretz.' I couldn't believe it—I thought he was dead. He replied, 'I am at least half-dead,' and later expressed sorrow about my parents. Even in that moment, I found myself saying it felt just like school again.

grounded_facts: Tuvia touches Shimon and verbally invites him to come with the group.
Tuvia physically touches Shimon and explicitly invites him to come with the followers, integrating him into the group.
memories.memory_text: I touched Shimon and said, 'Teacher... Come... Come. Please,' inviting him to join us in the forest for safety and survival.

grounded_facts: Survivors gather around a fire to share soup and cooked potatoes, though resources are scarce.
memories.memory_text: I saw the survivors gathered around the fire, sharing soup and cooked potatoes, though there weren't enough spoons for everyone.

grounded_facts: Shimon offers food to Aron, showing concern for his well-being.
memories.memory_text: I watched Shimon offer food to Aron and ask him if he wasn't hungry, clearly concerned for the boy's well-being.

grounded_facts: Aron does not respond when offered food, indicating emotional withdrawal or trauma.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Aron didn't respond when Shimon offered him food, and when Shimon asked if the little one would not talk, it was clear the boy was withdrawn or traumatized.

grounded_facts: Tuvia shows Zus the gun with only four bullets, establishing scarcity of resources.
memories.memory_text: I showed Zus the gun and told him there were only four bullets left, making it clear how little we had to defend everyone.

grounded_facts: Zus criticizes Tuvia for bringing more people without securing food, questioning his leadership.
memories.memory_text: I remember Zus confronting me, saying he sent me for food but I brought more mouths to feed, and later telling me we'd have to make the bullets count, questioning my choices.

grounded_facts: Shimon uses pages from a Hebrew book to start a fire, symbolizing sacrifice of sacred text for survival.
memories.memory_text: I saw Shimon take a Hebrew book from his coat, rip out the pages, and use them to start the fire, saying, 'The Psalms have many uses,' which struck me as a heavy sacrifice for survival.

grounded_facts: Avram digs a grave for his daughter, who died in Tuvia's absence.
memories.memory_text: I saw Avram digging a grave for his daughter, and I realized she had died while I was away.

grounded_facts: Tuvia stands in the rain, visibly shaken, observing the lit windows of a farmhouse at dusk.
memories.memory_text: I stand in the driving rain, shaking, staring at the lit windows of the farmhouse as dusk falls.

grounded_facts: The Police Captain attempts to justify his cooperation with the SS by citing job security and past leniency toward Tuvia's family.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Police Captain try to justify himself, saying it was his job and that he had been lenient with my family, but those words meant nothing to me.

grounded_facts: Tuvia enters the Police Captain's home, confronts him about his role in hunting Jews, and forces him to kneel at gunpoint.
Tuvia commands the Police Captain to kneel at gunpoint, escalating the confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I stood in the doorway, rain dripping from my coat, and made the Police Captain kneel at gunpoint because I knew he had hunted Jews and I could not let that go unpunished.

grounded_facts: Tuvia names his murdered parents and brothers, framing his actions as vengeance.
memories.memory_text: I named my murdered parents, David and Beila Bielski, and my brothers, speaking for them as I carried out my vengeance.

grounded_facts: After the Police Captain attempts to rise and one son moves toward him, Tuvia shoots and kills the son, the Police Captain, and then the other son.
memories.memory_text: I shot the son when he moved toward me, then the Police Captain as he started to rise, and then the other son.

grounded_facts: Tuvia contemplates killing the police captain's wife to prevent her from identifying him after the massacre.
memories.memory_text: I considered killing her to keep her from identifying me after the massacre.

grounded_facts: Tuvia orders the mourning wife to state who committed the killings, creating a moment of psychological pressure.
Tuvia commands the grieving wife to reveal who committed the massacre, possibly testing her knowledge or asserting control.
memories.memory_text: I told the grieving wife to tell them who did this, putting pressure on her in that moment.

grounded_facts: Tuvia flees from the police captain's house during heavy rain.
memories.memory_text: I fled from the police captain's house during heavy rain, running as the downpour soaked through my clothes.

grounded_facts: Tuvia confesses to God that he has committed murder, justifying it by deeming his victims as undeserving of life.
memories.memory_text: I confessed to God that I have committed murder, asking for forgiveness because I believed those I killed were monsters who did not deserve to live.

grounded_facts: The group awakens the morning after a violent encounter, assessing losses and planning next steps in a low fog-covered forest.
memories.memory_text: I woke up that morning with the group huddled together in the fog, counting how many of us were left after the fight.

grounded_facts: Zus takes the pistol from Tuvia's belt and checks the ammunition, noting only one bullet remains.
memories.memory_text: I remember sitting by the fire when Zus took the pistol from my belt and checked the cylinder, then said, 'Only one bullet left.'

grounded_facts: Zus asks Tuvia if it felt good to kill his sons, prompting Tuvia to tell him to shut up.
memories.memory_text: I told Zus to shut up when he asked if it felt good to kill his sons.

grounded_facts: Zus raises concerns about the women and the old teacher slowing them down; Tuvia responds with sarcasm but ultimately agrees on the need for mobility.
memories.memory_text: I remember Zus asking what we’d do with the others, worried the women and my old teacher would slow us down, and me snapping back with sarcasm about homework—but in the end, I agreed we needed to stay mobile.

grounded_facts: Zus and Tuvia agree to leave behind the women and the old teacher by moving their camp farther up the trail, exposing the others to potential capture or death.
memories.memory_text: I decided we should sleep farther up the trail, knowing that if anyone came, they’d find the others first and the gunshots would give us time to escape, even though it meant leaving them behind.

grounded_facts: Tuvia introduces the new arrivals to the group, establishing their identities and connections.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia introduces the new arrivals to the group, establishing their identities and connections.

grounded_facts: Tuvia presents the new arrivals to the camp, emphasizing familial and personal connections.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia presents the new arrivals to the camp, emphasizing familial and personal connections.

grounded_facts: Zus challenges Tuvia’s decision to bring more people by questioning how they will feed them.
Zus expresses concern about the group's ability to feed the growing number of people.
memories.memory_text: I remember Zus pulling me aside and telling me he has pity for the new people, but then demanding to know how we’ll feed them all — I told him we’d water the soup to make it stretch.

grounded_facts: Several refugees, including Tamara, Lazar, Isaac Malbin, and a dark-haired beauty, arrive at the camp under Tuvia's escort.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Several refugees, including Tamara, Lazar, Isaac Malbin, and a dark-haired beauty, arrive at the camp under Tuvia's escort.

grounded_facts: A gathering upon the arrival of new refugees, involving introductions, integration attempts, and immediate questioning by veterans.
memories.memory_text: I remember that A gathering upon the arrival of new refugees, involving introductions, integration attempts, and immediate questioning by veterans.

grounded_facts: Existing camp members ask the newcomers for news from their hometowns, seeking information about survivors.
memories.memory_text: I saw the veterans questioning the newcomers, asking about people from their hometowns, trying to find out who might have survived.

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Malbin attempt to build a shelter, highlighting Malbin's lack of practical skills.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia and Malbin attempt to build a shelter, highlighting Malbin's lack of practical skills.

grounded_facts: Malbin discloses he is an intellectual who published a small journal, contrasting with the physical labor required in the camp.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Malbin discloses he is an intellectual who published a small journal, contrasting with the physical labor required in the camp.

grounded_facts: Two starving young men emerge from the forest armed, demanding food and briefly holding the camp at gunpoint.
memories.memory_text: I saw two starving young men emerge from the forest, one of them pointing a rifle at us and demanding food, and I felt the tension rise as the situation turned dangerous.

grounded_facts: Zus defiantly challenges the young man's courage to shoot him, escalating tension.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Zus defiantly challenging the armed young man, shouting at him to shoot, which made the whole camp hold its breath in fear.

grounded_facts: Tuvia calms the situation by inviting the newcomers to sit and share food.
memories.memory_text: I stepped in and told the newcomers they could share our food, inviting them to sit down and put their guns away to calm things down.

grounded_facts: Two young survivors from Horodyszcze arrive at the camp, bringing news of the massacre and triggering emotional revelations.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Two young survivors from Horodyszcze arrive at the camp, bringing news of the massacre and triggering emotional revelations.

grounded_facts: Zus desperately asks if the survivor knew his wife Sonia and their child.
Zus discovers from survivors that his wife Sonia and child are likely dead, leading to an emotional breakdown.
memories.memory_text: I saw Zus ask the survivor if he knew Sonia and their child, and when he realized they were gone, I watched him break down and beat his head against a tree until blood poured down his face.

grounded_facts: Tuvia embraces Zus as he grieves the loss of his family.
memories.memory_text: I put my arms around my brother as he sobbed, holding him tight to comfort him in his grief, even when he eventually pulled away.

grounded_facts: A group gathers by a fire to discuss joining or forming a partisan unit, leading to declarations of identity and intent.
memories.memory_text: I heard from others by the fire that the Russians are beginning to organize, and we discussed whether to join them or form our own unit.

grounded_facts: Asael declares the group as the Bielski Otriad, establishing their identity as a partisan unit.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Asael declare right there that we are the Bielski Otriad and ask if anyone wanted to join.

grounded_facts: Tuvia urges Zus not to pursue revenge killings, warning that they must not become like their enemies.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia urges Zus not to pursue revenge killings, warning that they must not become like their enemies.

grounded_facts: Zus loads Wilencki's gun and indicates he is forming a group, including Peretz, Jacov, and Asael, to take action, signaling a shift in leadership and intent to act independently of Tuvia.
memories.memory_text: I saw Zus load Wilencki's gun and say he was taking Peretz, Jacov, and Asael with him, making it clear they were going to act without me.

grounded_facts: A tense ideological and leadership confrontation between Tuvia and Zus just outside the camp, centered on retaliation, morality, and command.
memories.memory_text: I remember the tension building outside the camp as Zus and I faced off—our argument wasn't just about who was in charge, but about whether we should retaliate with blood for blood or hold back our rage.

grounded_facts: Zus questions Tuvia's authority by asking 'You are making the decisions now?' after revealing he has formed a group to act without Tuvia's approval.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Zus, asking him directly, 'You are making the decisions now?' when he announced his group was moving out on their own.

grounded_facts: Tuvia ends the confrontation by declaring they will wait for dark, reasserting his authority over timing and strategy despite the challenge from Zus.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia ends the confrontation by declaring they will wait for dark, reasserting his authority over timing and strategy despite the challenge from Zus.

grounded_facts: Tuvia reveals that he and his group were responsible for burning the man's truck.
memories.memory_text: I told him, 'We did,' making it clear to the man that I was responsible for burning his truck.

grounded_facts: Zus opens fire on the man after he pleads, followed by Jacov and Peretz, resulting in the man's death.
memories.memory_text: I saw Zus open fire after the man pleaded, and then Jacov and Peretz shot him too—I watched him go down.

grounded_facts: A confrontation between the partisans and a former collaborator at the site of a burning truck.
memories.memory_text: I was there when we confronted the man at his burning truck, stepping out of the shadows with Zus and the others as he ran from the tavern.

grounded_facts: The partisans burn a truck and kill the man who previously transported Jews, disposing of his body on the burning vehicle.
memories.memory_text: I was there when we ambushed the man who had betrayed us; I saw Zus fire, and I helped throw his body onto the burning truck.

grounded_facts: Tuvia becomes concerned that Zus's actions and speech are drawing excessive attention and risking broader exposure or retaliation.
memories.memory_text: I looked around and saw how people were reacting — this is getting out of hand, and I realized Zus's actions and words are drawing too much attention, putting us all at risk.

grounded_facts: Tuvia attaches one end of a wire to a post beside the road, likely preparing a trap or signal.
memories.memory_text: I attached one end of the wire to a post beside the road while lying in the ditch with Asael, setting up a trap or warning signal.

grounded_facts: Tuvia tightens a wire across the road to create an invisible trap as a bike approaches.
memories.memory_text: I tightened the wire across the road just as the bike was approaching, making it invisible to trap whoever was coming.

grounded_facts: The motorcyclist is garroted by a wire, and the Bielskis kill him with the last bullet from the Mahkarov.
memories.memory_text: I saw the motorcyclist go down when we used the wire and finished him with the last bullet from the Mahkarov.

grounded_facts: Peretz spots approaching headlights and alerts the others.
memories.memory_text: I saw Peretz alert the group when he spotted approaching headlights, and then I noticed more headlights coming fast.

grounded_facts: Upon seeing more headlights approaching, Tuvia orders everyone to hide, and they retreat into the ditch, taking the dead courier with them.
Tuvia issues an urgent order to hide upon sighting approaching headlights.
memories.memory_text: I ordered everyone to hide when I saw the headlights approaching, and we scrambled into the ditch, taking the dead courier with us.

grounded_facts: Tuvia tackles the Lieutenant as he reaches for his pistol, leading to a physical struggle.
memories.memory_text: I tackled the Lieutenant just as he went for his gun, and we ended up fighting on the road—I punched, clawed, and slammed his head into the pavement to stop him.

grounded_facts: Zus kills the officer who was about to shoot Tuvia, thereby saving his brother's life.
Zus turns the machine gun on the staff car, blowing out the windows and killing the officer and woman inside.
memories.memory_text: I rolled under the car to avoid being shot, and I saw Zus turn the machine gun on the staff car, blowing out the windows and killing the officer and the woman, which saved my life.

grounded_facts: Zus uses the knife handle to break the sergeant's nose and takes his Schmeisser, then kills him with it.
A violent confrontation occurs around the staff car involving gunfire, weapon seizure, and rescue.
memories.memory_text: I rolled under the staff car to avoid the gunfire, and I saw Zus use the knife handle to break the sergeant's nose, rip the Schmeisser from him, and shoot him point-blank, then turn the gun on the car to save my life.

grounded_facts: Zus hands the Schmeisser to Tuvia as a symbolic and practical gesture of trust and shared victory.
memories.memory_text: Zus handed me the Schmeisser like it was a trophy, a sign that he trusted me and saw me as part of the victory.

grounded_facts: Tuvia is given a Schmeisser submachine gun by Zus after the killing, which he accepts and checks efficiently.
memories.memory_text: I took the Schmeisser from Zus and checked it over quickly, making sure it was in working order.

grounded_facts: Jacov tosses a bottle of schnapps to Tuvia, celebrating the successful ambush.
memories.memory_text: I caught a bottle of schnapps Jacov tossed to me as we celebrated the ambush.

grounded_facts: Peretz and Jacov search the staff car and retrieve machine-pistols, schnapps, and a camera.
memories.memory_text: I saw Peretz and Jacov search the staff car and come back with machine-pistols, bottles of schnapps, and a camera.

grounded_facts: Tuvia shouts at Jacov to stop firing, recognizing the futility and danger of resistance.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at Jacov to stop firing because I knew it would only get him killed.

grounded_facts: Jacov is killed by machine gun fire after opening fire on approaching troops.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jacov cut down by machine gun fire after he opened fire on the troops.

grounded_facts: Tuvia, Peretz, and Zus flee into the wheat field to escape gunfire.
memories.memory_text: I shouted for everyone to run into the fields, and I pulled Peretz off the road before racing with him and Zus into the wheat field to escape the gunfire.

grounded_facts: A flare ignites overhead, brightly lighting the wheat field and increasing exposure.
memories.memory_text: I saw a flare ignite overhead, turning the wheat field bright white and exposing us as we ran.

grounded_facts: Asael flees into the wheat field on the wrong side of the road, becoming isolated and exposed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael run into the wheat field on the wrong side of the road, and I knew he was exposed and alone.

grounded_facts: A military truck moves to block Asael's escape route and uses a spotlight to expose him.
memories.memory_text: I watched a military truck move forward and cut off Asael's path, shining a spotlight on him so everyone could see.

grounded_facts: Peretz is wounded while converging on the target, causing him to fall before being assisted by Tuvia and Zus.
memories.memory_text: I saw Peretz get hit while we were moving forward, and I helped him up with Zus so we could carry him into the forest.

grounded_facts: Tuvia gives a brief order to Zus to retrieve Peretz's rifle.
memories.memory_text: I gave Zus a quick order to go back for Peretz's rifle after he was hit.

grounded_facts: Zus returns to collect Peretz's dropped rifle after he is wounded.
memories.memory_text: I saw Zus return to pick up Peretz's dropped rifle after we got him into the woods.

grounded_facts: Tuvia forcibly takes the rifle from Zus upon seeing Asael in danger, indicating a shift in his intention to intervene.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael in danger and I took the rifle from Zus—I had to act, so I seized it and wedged it into the tree to take aim.

grounded_facts: Asael uses the darkness to hide, crawling and digging into the mud of an irrigation ditch to avoid capture.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael dive into the irrigation ditch and start crawling, digging into the mud to hide when the darkness gave him cover.

grounded_facts: Aron gives his ration of bread to Rachel, creating a small but meaningful human connection amid hardship.
memories.memory_text: I saw Aron give his bread ration to Rachel, a small act that made a connection between them despite the hardship we're all enduring.

grounded_facts: Shimon presses Tuvia on why no food was brought back, invoking moral responsibility from the Talmud.
memories.memory_text: I was confronted by Shimon, who asked me why no food was brought back and told me that the Talmud says saving a life means taking responsibility for it.

grounded_facts: Ben Zion enters the camp and asks to speak with the Bielskis, initiating contact.
memories.memory_text: I was present when a man entered the camp and asked, 'You are the Bielski's?'—he wanted to speak with me and my brothers, initiating contact.

grounded_facts: Zus discovers Lazar failed to stop a stranger from entering the camp and physically attacks him in a drunken rage.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Zus was drunk and must have found out Lazar let someone past the guard post, and I realized he’d started beating him up.

grounded_facts: Aron gives his bread ration to Rachel, forming a personal connection.
memories.memory_text: I saw Aron give his bread ration to Rachel—little enough to go around, but I noticed it, and it seemed like more than just sharing food.

grounded_facts: A dawn gathering of the group in the forest camp marked by hunger, despair, and a security breach.
memories.memory_text: I watched someone scrape the empty pot for porridge and saw others staring listlessly around; I shouted 'No' and later 'Enough!' as the weight of our hunger and the security breach pressed on me.

grounded_facts: Tuvia reminds Zus of the consequences of failure by referencing a hypothetical execution of Asael, deepening their conflict.
memories.memory_text: I reminded Zus that if we make mistakes, they will torture Asael and then hang him, making it clear that failure is not an option.

grounded_facts: Tuvia physically intervenes to stop Zus from continuing his attack on Lazar, asserting authority over his brother.
memories.memory_text: I pulled Zus off Lazar to stop the attack, and when he tried again, I yanked him back hard and left him on the ground to assert my authority.

grounded_facts: Ben Zion introduces himself by name after recognizing Tuvia, initiating personal connection and shared history.
memories.memory_text: I recognized Ben Zion when he introduced himself, and I knew our shared past meant he trusted me.

grounded_facts: Miriam asks Ben Zion if he knows her sister in Vilna, revealing personal loss and anxiety.
memories.memory_text: I heard Miriam ask Ben Zion about her sister in Vilna, and I could feel her anxiety as she spoke.

grounded_facts: Aron speaks for the first time, naming Asael as another lost friend, deepening the group's shared grief.
Aron breaks his silence by naming Asael, acknowledging another loss and prompting Tuvia to reaffirm the value of every life.
memories.memory_text: I heard Aron speak for the first time when he said, 'Or Asael,' naming another friend we lost, and in that moment I felt the weight of every life we carry.

grounded_facts: A gathering in the camp after Tuvia returns, where survivors express grief, debate their situation, and respond to Tuvia's leadership.
memories.memory_text: After I returned, I stood among the survivors as they grieved and looked to me, and I knew I had to offer them a vision of our future together.

grounded_facts: Tuvia looks directly at Zus while asserting collective unity, daring him to object, marking a power confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I looked directly at Zus while speaking, daring him to object, and I saw him lower his head when everyone else nodded in agreement.

grounded_facts: Tuvia overcomes initial awkwardness to deliver a unifying vision, establishing himself as the undisputed leader of the group by emphasizing survival with dignity, collective responsibility, and restraint in actions.
memories.memory_text: I overcame my awkwardness and spoke my vision—I told the group that we must survive with dignity, take care of each other, and not become like our enemies, and I felt the shift in the group as they accepted me as their leader.

grounded_facts: Tuvia, Zus, and Ben Zion leave their cover in the woods and cautiously approach KosciK's farm with guns ready.
memories.memory_text: I led Zus and Ben Zion as we left our cover in the woods and approached KosciK's farm cautiously, my gun ready.

grounded_facts: Koscik's wife gives a terse, unfriendly reply to Tuvia's greeting, showing reluctance but providing necessary information.
memories.memory_text: I saw Koscik's wife glare at me when I greeted her, and she gave me a short, unfriendly reply, though she still told me what I needed to know.

grounded_facts: Koscik's wife, without greeting or warmth, informs Tuvia in Russian that someone or something is in the barn.
memories.memory_text: I was told in Russian that whatever we were looking for is in the barn.

grounded_facts: Tuvia expresses sorrow to Koscik's wife after completing the burial.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Koscik's wife and told her, 'I'm sorry,' feeling the weight of her loss.

grounded_facts: Tuvia finishes burying Koscik after digging the grave, marking the end of the burial process.
The burial ceremony of Koscik, conducted near a barn with Tuvia and Koscik's wife present.
memories.memory_text: I finished burying Koscik near the barn, piling the last shovelful of earth onto his grave while his wife stood there, staring ahead.

grounded_facts: Koscik's wife, in a monotone, tells Tuvia to come along, signaling the end of the burial moment.
memories.memory_text: I heard Koscik's wife say 'Come' in a flat voice, and I knew it was time to leave.

grounded_facts: Asael comes out of the hidden root cellar into the light, reuniting with his brothers after being lost.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael emerge from the root cellar, blinking into the light, and my heart leapt—he was alive.

grounded_facts: Zus tightly hugs his long-lost brother Asael in an emotional reunion.
memories.memory_text: I watched Zus pull Asael into a tight embrace, holding him like he'd never let go.

grounded_facts: A gathering at the root cellar where Asael reunites with his brothers and reveals those he was hiding with.
memories.memory_text: I stood with my brothers at the root cellar as Asael returned, and I saw how deeply moved everyone was, including me when I turned to Koscik's wife.

grounded_facts: Tuvia expresses deep gratitude to Koscik's wife for her help in sheltering Asael and others.
memories.memory_text: I turned to Koscik's wife, deeply moved, and told her thank you for helping shelter Asael and the others.

grounded_facts: Tuvia tests Asael's attention by asking him Chaya's name, verifying his awareness.
memories.memory_text: I tested Asael's attention by asking him what her name was, and he replied, 'Chaya.'

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Asael discuss intelligence and mission plans in the camp, including village patrols, informers, and supply locations.
memories.memory_text: I discussed with Asael what we need to know about the villages, the German patrols, and the informers, and I asked him whose turn it was to go out.

grounded_facts: Tuvia decides that Asael should accompany Zus on the mission to ensure his orders are followed.
memories.memory_text: I decided Asael should go with Zus on the mission to make sure my orders are followed.

grounded_facts: Tuvia notices Asael's distraction by Chaya and calls attention to it, then encourages him to talk to her.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Asael wasn't listening because he was watching Chaya walk by, so I asked if he was paying attention and then told him to go talk to her.

grounded_facts: Prompted by Tuvia, Asael begins walking toward Chaya to talk to her.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael begin walking toward Chaya after I encouraged him to go talk to her.

grounded_facts: A group gathers by a fire where newcomers are being shown around, music is played, and personal interactions occur.
memories.memory_text: I saw Ben Zion showing the newcomers around our camp, and later someone played a violin by the fire—I felt the weight of what we've lost, but I had to stay composed for everyone.

grounded_facts: Tuvia is informed by Ben Zion that his wife was killed last week, according to newcomers from Novagroduk.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Ben Zion that the newcomers from Novagroduk said my wife was killed last week, and he expressed his sorrow.

grounded_facts: Malbin quotes Descartes; Shimon responds with a humorous twist.
memories.memory_text: I was told about the new people from Novagroduk, and I thanked Ben Zion for informing me, though it brought back the pain of losing my wife just last week.

grounded_facts: After learning of his wife's death, Tuvia suppresses grief and redirects conversation to practical matters.
memories.memory_text: After hearing about my wife, I thanked Ben Zion and immediately turned the conversation to digging a trench around the new zemylanka because I couldn't face the grief.

grounded_facts: Shimon expresses sympathy for Tuvia's loss and gently suggests reciting the Kaddish.
memories.memory_text: Shimon expressed his sympathy and suggested we recite the Kaddish together, his voice soft with care.

grounded_facts: A moment of quiet mourning following the death of Tuvia's wife, marked by Shimon's presence and offer to recite Kaddish.
memories.memory_text: I stood in silence after my wife passed, and Shimon came to offer his condolences, saying he was sorry for my loss and gently asking if I wanted to say the Kaddish.

grounded_facts: Tuvia reflects on the complex and strained relationship with his deceased wife, expressing grief mixed with unresolved resentment.
memories.memory_text: When I spoke, it was barely a whisper—I thought of how strained and distant we had become, how my grief is tangled with old resentment.

grounded_facts: Tuvia discloses the emotional coldness and failure of his marriage, reframing his grief.
memories.memory_text: I finally spoke, almost to myself—she was a beautiful woman, but cold, and not a day went by she didn't remind me I wasn't a good provider. Our marriage hadn't been real for years.

grounded_facts: Zus shouts for absolute silence, likely to avoid detection during the attack.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus shout for absolute silence to avoid detection when the shooting started.

grounded_facts: Tuvia takes charge during the attack, ordering people to follow Asael and maintain movement.
memories.memory_text: I took charge during the attack, shouting that only food and guns should be carried, and I ordered everyone to follow Asael while I urged him to keep the group moving without stopping.

grounded_facts: Asael takes responsibility for moving people to safety, holding Chaya's hand while organizing the evacuation.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael take responsibility for getting people out safely, holding Chaya's hand as he led them, and I made sure to tell him to keep them moving.

grounded_facts: The policemen open fire on the camp, killing two people and raking a shelter with a submachine gun, marking the start of a violent assault.
memories.memory_text: I saw the policemen open fire, killing two of our people, and I pushed others deeper into the woods as they raked a shelter with a submachine gun—I knew we had to get everyone out immediately.

grounded_facts: Kissely locates the pre-existing escape route into the woods, enabling the group's retreat.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Kissely had found the escape trail into the woods, and he called out for us to follow.

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Zus lead the group across the river and up the embankment to escape pursuing forces.
memories.memory_text: I led the group across the river and up the embankment with Zus, shouting orders to keep everyone moving.

grounded_facts: As the policemen cross the river, shots ring out; one policeman is killed, and a German soldier is wounded and dragged from the water.
memories.memory_text: I saw the shots ring out as the policemen crossed the river—I watched one fall and a German soldier get dragged from the water after being hit.

grounded_facts: From cover, Zus shouts a warning in Russian, threatening to shoot if the policemen do not retreat.
Zus issues a verbal threat from cover, warning the policemen to leave or be shot.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus shout from cover in Russian, warning them to leave or be shot, and then he called out that there were hundreds of us, trying to make them think we were stronger than we were.

grounded_facts: Tuvia questions Kissely's loyalty, accusing him of betraying his own people by working for the Germans.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Kissely, demanding to know why he, a man from Belarussia, would work for the Germans against his own people, and he told me it was to survive—just like I steal from the poor.

grounded_facts: An armed standoff occurs between the Bielski partisans and collaborating policemen, involving gunfire, verbal threats, and psychological tactics.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the armed standoff with the collaborating policemen—them crossing the river, shouting demands, and firing shots, one of which hit Kessely in the arm.

grounded_facts: Kissely is shot in the arm during the standoff, escalating the violence.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kissely get shot in the arm during the standoff—the shot rang out and the violence escalated further.

grounded_facts: After the retreat, Tuvia acknowledges the need to relocate the camp due to compromised safety.
memories.memory_text: I said they'll be back, and I knew we had to find a new camp because our safety was compromised.

grounded_facts: After the retreat of the policemen, the Bielski brothers and comrades reassemble to assess the situation and plan next steps.
memories.memory_text: After the policemen retreated, I emerged with Zus and the others, saw the dead German, and knew they would return, so I said we had to find a new camp.

grounded_facts: Zus directly criticizes Tuvia's leadership and policy of mercy, blaming it for their current vulnerability.
Zus confronts Tuvia about his diplomatic approach, blaming it for their vulnerability and lack of shelter.
memories.memory_text: I remember Zus confronting me, shouting that my policy of diplomacy is shit and that we should have killed the milkman — he blamed my restraint for leaving us vulnerable and without shelter.

grounded_facts: The group rests on a hillside, recovering energy and sharing limited resources.
memories.memory_text: I walked among the group as we rested on the hillside, seeing how little energy they had left and how we shared what little we had.

grounded_facts: Tuvia requests volunteers for a scouting party after the group rests.
Tuvia calls for volunteers for a scouting mission, and Zus responds immediately.
memories.memory_text: After we rested, I called for volunteers for a scouting party, and I saw Zus raise his hand immediately.

grounded_facts: A confrontation between Tuvia's group and a unit of Red Army soldiers in the forest.
memories.memory_text: I saw Red Army soldiers step out of the forest and surround us with their rifles drawn.

grounded_facts: Tuvia asserts that he and his group are part of the Bielski otriad when confronted by Red Army soldiers.
memories.memory_text: I told the Red Army soldier that we belong to the Bielski otriad to keep us safe.

grounded_facts: Gramov labels Tuvia's group as 'Jewish bandits,' escalating tension.
memories.memory_text: I heard Gramov call us 'Jewish bandits,' and I could feel the tension rise between us.

grounded_facts: Zus tenses and indicates readiness to shoot two of the surrounding soldiers.
memories.memory_text: I saw Zus tense up and tighten his finger on the trigger of his submachine gun, ready to shoot two of the soldiers around us.

grounded_facts: Tuvia attempts to defuse tension by proposing to clarify the situation with Gramov's commander.
memories.memory_text: I tried to calm the situation by suggesting we clear up the misunderstanding with Gramov's commander.

grounded_facts: Viktor Panchenko accuses Tuvia's group of being a Jewish gang that steals from villages loyal to the partisans.
Viktor formally accuses Tuvia's group of stealing from loyal villages.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Viktor that he accused my group of being a Jewish gang that steals from villages loyal to the partisans, and he formally charged us with theft during the meeting.

grounded_facts: Tuvia counters Viktor's claim that Jews do not fight by asserting that his group does fight.
Tuvia rejects Viktor's implication that Jews do not fight by asserting their combat role.
memories.memory_text: I countered Viktor's claim that Jews don't fight by telling him, 'These Jews do,' making it clear that my group and I are fighters who resist.

grounded_facts: Viktor orders Tuvia to send his best fighters to prove their value.
Viktor commands Tuvia to send his best fighters as proof of their worth.
memories.memory_text: I heard Viktor demand that I send my best fighters to prove our worth, as if our survival and struggle meant nothing to him.

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Zus salute and agree to serve, acknowledging their lack of alternatives.
memories.memory_text: I saluted alongside Zus and we turned to leave, knowing we had to accept this role.

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Zus meet Viktor Panchenko, commander of the October otriad, to negotiate their group's status.
memories.memory_text: I met Viktor Panchenko with Zus to negotiate our group's place among the partisans, and I could feel the tension as soon as he emerged from the tent.

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Zus acknowledge their forced integration into the partisan structure.
memories.memory_text: I realized we were being forced into the partisan structure, as if we had no choice but to comply.

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Malbin collaborate on building a new bunker at Camp #2, combining physical labor with conversation about leadership and values.
memories.memory_text: I worked alongside Malbin on the new bunker at Camp #2, laboring together while talking about our roles and what we stood for.

grounded_facts: Malbin comments wistfully that his former intellectual friends would not recognize him now, signaling internal tension between past identity and present role.
memories.memory_text: I heard Malbin say wistfully, 'If my friends at The New Socialists' Club could see me now,' and I could sense the tension in his voice about who he used to be versus who he is now.

grounded_facts: Tuvia admits he was not a good student, referencing Shimon as a witness to his past academic struggles.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Malbin that I wasn't a very good student, and I told him he could ask Shimon to confirm it, because I wanted him to know I don't hide my past.

grounded_facts: When questioned why he accepts Tuvia as commander despite their differing backgrounds, Malbin responds pragmatically: 'Who else?'
memories.memory_text: I asked Malbin why he accepts me as commander despite our different backgrounds, and when he simply replied 'Who else?', I understood that leadership isn't about education but about necessity.

grounded_facts: Malbin asks permission to share a critical thought about the group's values, introducing the idea that strength is not the only priority.
memories.memory_text: Malbin asked me if he could share an observation, and I remember him suggesting that strength isn't the only thing we should value.

grounded_facts: Malbin articulates 'community' as an important principle for the group, prompting Tuvia to reflect.
memories.memory_text: I heard Malbin say 'community' as he introduced it as a key principle, and I began to reflect on what that truly meant for us.

grounded_facts: After Malbin suggests community as a value, Tuvia asks if he has more ideas, showing openness to collaborative leadership.
Tuvia recognizes Malbin’s intellectual contribution and invites further ideas, signaling openness to shared leadership.
memories.memory_text: I acknowledged Malbin's insight about community and asked if he had more ideas, letting him know I was listening and open to his thoughts on how we should lead together.

grounded_facts: Shulman kisses the ground upon arrival and then seeks out Tuvia, kissing his hand to show reverence and recognition of leadership.
memories.memory_text: When Shulman arrived, he kissed the ground and then came to me, asking 'Which one is Tuvia Bielski?' before kissing my hand, showing me a reverence I didn’t ask for but felt deeply.

grounded_facts: A group of new arrivals, including Yitzhak Shulman, is brought into the camp by Asael, prompting emotional and informational reactions from the existing group.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael bring in a group of new arrivals, including a young man named Yitzhak Shulman, and I could feel the weight of their journey in the way they moved.

grounded_facts: Yitzhak Shulman arrives in the camp, removes his Star of David, kisses the ground, identifies Tuvia Bielski, and reports that the Baranowicze ghetto is about to be liquidated.
memories.memory_text: Shulman told me he was from Baranowicze and that the ghetto there was about to be liquidated, and in that moment, I knew we had to act.

grounded_facts: When Shulman attempts to kiss Tuvia’s hand again, Tuvia instead takes his hand and shakes it, transforming the gesture into one of equality.
memories.memory_text: When Shulman tried to kiss my hand again, I took it instead and shook it firmly, wanting him to know we were equals in this struggle.

grounded_facts: Zus observes a glance between Tuvia and Malbin, recognizing Malbin's growing sway over Tuvia's decisions.
memories.memory_text: I exchanged a glance with Malbin, and I knew Zus had seen it—he must have sensed something shifting between us.

grounded_facts: Zus sarcastically addresses Tuvia as 'Pan Tuvia' and 'Rabbi Tuvia', questioning his authority and motives.
Zus sarcastically offers to kiss Tuvia's hand, ridiculing his self-importance.
memories.memory_text: Zus mocked me, calling me 'Pan Tuvia' and 'Rabbi Tuvia' while grabbing my hand, pretending he wanted to kiss it—I tried to pull away, but he held on tight.

grounded_facts: Zus questions the feasibility and wisdom of Tuvia's plan to rescue more Jews.
Zus challenges Tuvia's decision to bring in more people from the ghetto, expressing fear that it will endanger the group.
memories.memory_text: I remember Zus confronting me, questioning whether it was wise to bring more Jews from the ghetto, fearing it would endanger our group and challenging the very purpose of our mission.

grounded_facts: Zus refers to the new Jewish refugees as 'Malbushim' and 'bloodsuckers', rejecting their worth and integration.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus call the new arrivals 'Malbushim' and 'bloodsuckers,' saying they were empty clothes and pretentious Jews who looked down on us before.

grounded_facts: Tuvia counters Zus's moral authority by questioning the authenticity of his relationship with Bella.
Tuvia implies that Zus's relationship with Bella is situational, not based on love.
memories.memory_text: I challenged Zus about Bella, asking him if she'd even be with him if it wasn't for the war, and I questioned whether it was really love between them.

grounded_facts: A heated argument between Zus and Tuvia over leadership, policy, and personal values escalates into physical violence.
memories.memory_text: I recall the argument escalating until Zus charged at me, and I slammed him in the gut, then we turned on Ben Zion when he tried to stop us—our brotherhood fracturing in that moment.

grounded_facts: Tuvia picks up a rock to strike Zus but stops himself at the last moment.
memories.memory_text: I picked up a rock to strike Zus, but I stopped myself at the last moment.

grounded_facts: The verbal conflict escalates into a violent brawl between the two brothers.
memories.memory_text: I tried to pull my hand away when Zus grabbed me, but he wouldn't let go, and then he punched me in the face — all the rage from years of rivalry exploded into fists, and when he got on top of me and started beating me, I rolled away desperate and grabbed a rock, ready to smash it into his head, but I stopped myself.

grounded_facts: Zus announces his departure to join real partisans, taking several men with him.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus call out to Ben Zion, Krensky, Lova, and Israel to leave with him, and then he told me directly that they were going to join the real partisans.

grounded_facts: Zus asks Asael to leave with him and join the real partisans.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus ask Asael to come with him and join the real partisans.

grounded_facts: When asked, Asael refuses to follow Zus, remaining loyal to Tuvia.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael refuse to follow Zus and stay by my side when asked.

grounded_facts: Zus forms a splinter group and leaves to join the real partisans, marking a permanent split from Tuvia.
memories.memory_text: I saw Zus gather Ben Zion, Krensky, Lova, and Israel, declaring they would join the real partisans, and I watched him touch Bella’s arm before disappearing down the trail, leaving me behind.

grounded_facts: Zus leaves the group, touching Bella's arm before disappearing down the trail with others.
Zus silently touches Bella's arm as a final gesture before departing.
memories.memory_text: I watched Zus touch Bella's arm and then disappear down the trail with his followers.

grounded_facts: Tuvia and Asael physically cross the wall of the Novogrudok ghetto, marking an escape or transition from confinement.
memories.memory_text: I climbed over the dilapidated wall of the Novogrudok ghetto with Asael, escaping from confinement.

grounded_facts: Tuvia consults a map and decides on a direction to proceed through the deserted streets.
memories.memory_text: I studied the hand-drawn map and decided we should go this way through the deserted streets.

grounded_facts: A gathering of ghetto elders and resistance leaders to discuss survival strategies amid Nazi occupation.
memories.memory_text: I was there with Asael, talking to several elders of the ghetto council about how we could survive under Nazi occupation.

grounded_facts: Tuvia suggests taking all the ghetto inhabitants, including the old and sick, to the partisans for protection.
memories.memory_text: I suggested to the elder that we take all of you—everyone in the ghetto, even the old and sick—to the partisans for protection.

grounded_facts: Tuvia forcefully responds to the elder's skepticism by emphasizing the limited time they have left.
memories.memory_text: I told the elders they could have a day, a month, maybe a year to live — I said it straight to them because they kept asking for time we don’t have.

grounded_facts: Tuvia seeks religious validation or support from the Rabbi after failing to convince the elders.
memories.memory_text: After the elders wouldn’t listen, I turned to the Rabbi and asked for his support, but he said they were waiting for God, not action.

grounded_facts: Lilka's declaration shifts the group dynamic from inaction to collective commitment.
memories.memory_text: I realized her words broke the hesitation in the room, though I wasn't sure yet if this shift would hold or if people would follow through.

grounded_facts: Lilka publicly declares her decision to leave the ghetto, triggering a cascade of similar declarations.
memories.memory_text: I saw Lilka stand up and say, 'I am going,' and then others quickly followed, declaring they were coming too.

grounded_facts: Tuvia takes Lilka's hand and helps her through the tunnel, sharing a brief moment of eye contact.
Tuvia takes Lilka's hand and helps her pass through the tunnel, sharing a brief eye contact.
memories.memory_text: I took Lilka's hand and helped her through the tunnel, meeting her eyes for a brief moment.

grounded_facts: Chaya is reunited with her parents upon their arrival at the forest camp.
memories.memory_text: I saw Chaya holding Asael's arm and looking up at him with absolute rapture when her parents arrived, though I wasn't sure exactly how they found each other.

grounded_facts: Malbin enforces the collection of valuables from new arrivals to be used by the collective.
Malbin insists the well-dressed woman surrender her jewelry for the collective.
memories.memory_text: I saw Malbin collect valuables from the new arrivals, and I remember him telling the well-dressed woman that her grandmother's jewelry now belonged to the otriad and that everyone must sacrifice for the collective.

grounded_facts: Shimon questions new arrivals to identify useful skills for camp labor.
memories.memory_text: I saw Shimon questioning the new arrivals to find out who had skills useful for the camp.

grounded_facts: Oppenheim, a watchmaker, successfully repairs a rifle trigger and is reassigned to work on guns.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Oppenheim, who said he was a watchmaker, successfully repair a rifle trigger when I gave him the challenge, and I reassigned him to work on guns.

grounded_facts: Tuvia challenges Oppenheim to fix a rifle trigger to assess his mechanical ability.
memories.memory_text: I challenged Oppenheim to fix a rifle trigger to test his mechanical skill, and after he succeeded, I told him, 'You have a new profession.'

grounded_facts: Shulman brings in a magnificent white horse found running free, which Tuvia mounts and uses to address the new arrivals.
memories.memory_text: I saw Shulman bring in a magnificent white horse that had been running free, and I mounted her to greet the new arrivals.

grounded_facts: A structured intake event where new refugees are welcomed, assessed, and integrated into the camp.
memories.memory_text: I rode my white horse around the perimeter, greeting the new arrivals and making sure they knew I was in charge.

grounded_facts: Tuvia uses the arrival of newcomers and the presence of the white horse to publicly assert his authority and set expectations.
Tuvia greets the new arrivals and informs them of camp rules and expectations.
memories.memory_text: I used the moment on horseback to assert my authority, making sure everyone knew I was in charge, and I told the new arrivals that they were welcome but that everyone must work and follow the rules.

grounded_facts: Asael is teaching members of the group how to use guns.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael teaching some of the members how to use guns, showing them the basics of handling and firing.

grounded_facts: Tuvia communicates the group's new mission to support the Russian Partisans through material contributions.
Tuvia announces a plan for the group to support Russian Partisans by making clothes and repairing guns.
memories.memory_text: I announced to the group that we would support the Russian Partisans by making clothes and repairing guns, declaring our new mission.

grounded_facts: People are being introduced to various tasks including shoemaking, sewing, cooking, and gun use under Asael's teaching.
memories.memory_text: I noticed people being introduced to different tasks like sewing, shoemaking, cooking, and gun use, though I'm not certain exactly who is learning what or how it's all organized.

grounded_facts: Malbin catches Tuvia's eye and winks, indicating their prior agreement on the strategy behind the announcements.
memories.memory_text: I saw Malbin catch my eye and wink, a silent confirmation that we were aligned on the strategy for the announcements I was about to make.

grounded_facts: Tuvia announces that women will be trained to use weapons and fight alongside men, symbolically elevating a rifle as a historical weapon of Jewish resistance.
memories.memory_text: I announced that women will learn to use weapons and fight alongside men, and when I took the rifle from Asael and held it high, I told them this is not just a gun—it is Bar Kochba's spear, Ehud's sword, our means to protect ourselves.

grounded_facts: Tuvia declares that pregnancies are forbidden due to lack of resources and overcrowded bunkers, requiring new construction.
memories.memory_text: I declared that pregnancies are forbidden because we can't support infants right now — our bunkers are overcrowded and resources are too scarce, so I told everyone new bunkers must be built.

grounded_facts: Tuvia declares the forest camp the only place in Belorussia where Jews can live freely, vowing to rebuild lost lives and welcoming newcomers into the community.
memories.memory_text: I declared that this forest is the only place in all of Belorussia where a Jew can be free, and I vowed that we would rebuild the lives that were taken from us, welcoming everyone into our community.

grounded_facts: A public assembly in the forest camp where Tuvia addresses the community, announces policies, and inspires collective identity.
memories.memory_text: I stood before the gathering, holding the rifle high, feeling the weight of every expectant face watching me, and I told them this forest is the one place in Belorussia where a Jew can be free — we would rebuild our lives here and welcome them into our community.

grounded_facts: Riva identifies Tuvia Bielski and acknowledges him as a hero, calling him a Maccabee, which leads to Tuvia reflecting positively on his image.
Riva verbally recognizes Tuvia as a heroic figure and shakes his hand vigorously.
memories.memory_text: I was stopped by Riva who looked at me closely and asked if I was really Tuvia Bielski; when she recognized me, she called me a hero and a Maccabee, then shook my hand vigorously, and I found myself reflecting on who I’ve become as I saw my face in the water afterward.

grounded_facts: She realizes Tuvia and others are watching her as she tears at her clothes, leading to intense embarrassment.
memories.memory_text: I was watching her as she tore at her clothes and started crying, and then she realized we were all looking, which made her visibly mortified.

grounded_facts: Tuvia rides by on horseback along the opposite bank, drawing the attention of the women, especially Lilka.
memories.memory_text: I rode past the riverbank on my horse and noticed the women watching me, especially Lilka, who couldn't take her eyes off me.

grounded_facts: Tuvia shifts his attention from the wedding ceremony to Lilka, who has washed and let down her hair, indicating a moment of personal recognition or emotional reconnection.
Tuvia stares at Lilka; she meets his gaze and then looks away, suggesting mutual awareness and subtle emotional tension.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Lilka had washed and let down her hair, and when I stared at her, she met my gaze and then looked away, and I felt something pass between us.

grounded_facts: A wedding ceremony where Asael marries the bride, including traditional elements such as the glass crushing.
memories.memory_text: I saw Asael kiss the bride and later crush the glass underfoot during the wedding ceremony.

grounded_facts: Asael informs Tuvia that food is nearly depleted and there are discussions about returning to the ghetto due to starvation and increased danger during supply missions.
Asael reports the dire food situation and growing pressure to return to the ghetto.
memories.memory_text: Asael told me there is talk of returning to the ghetto because food is nearly gone and our supply missions face armed patrols, with farmers now guarding their barns with shotguns.

grounded_facts: Asael and Tuvia discuss the critical food shortage and potential return to the ghetto in a storage area.
memories.memory_text: I was in the storage area with Asael when he showed me the last few potatoes and told me people were talking about returning to the ghetto because they've barely eaten in days and even the farmers who once helped us now guard their barns with shotguns.

grounded_facts: Tuvia decides against returning to the ghetto and instead commands that more food-gathering missions be sent, now equipped with shotguns.
Tuvia orders more food missions and instructs them to bring shotguns.
memories.memory_text: I decided we cannot return to the ghetto, so I ordered more food missions to be sent out and told them to bring shotguns.

grounded_facts: Tuvia releases his horse from the stable, implying its slaughter to feed the starving group.
memories.memory_text: I visited my horse in the stable and untied him, knowing what had to be done to keep the group alive.

grounded_facts: The group whispers about the origin of the meat while eating, implicitly questioning Tuvia's actions.
The group receives and eats meat, sparking whispered speculation about its origin, implying moral weight and emotional consequence.
memories.memory_text: I watched them eat hungrily and heard the whispers—'Where'd it come from?'—knowing they were questioning the source of the meat.

grounded_facts: Meat is distributed in the food line, prompting hushed speculation among the group about its source.
memories.memory_text: I watched the group eat the meat distributed in the food line and heard their hushed whispers about what kind it was and where it came from.

grounded_facts: Zus sarcastically refers to his brother Tuvia as 'The Great Tuvia Bielski' and 'Big Shit', revealing resentment and rivalry.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zus mock me as 'The Great Tuvia Bielski' and 'Big Shit' while he was drinking, his tone full of resentment.

grounded_facts: Viktor discloses that his older brother was killed in the first hour of the German invasion, shifting the mood from drunken banter to somber reflection.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Viktor's older brother was killed in the first hour of the German invasion, which quieted the mood.

grounded_facts: Tuvia notices Lilka's distant state and gently inquires, showing concern.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Lilka seemed distant and shivering, so I gently called her name to check on her, and she said she was just thinking and that it was nothing.

grounded_facts: Lilka admits she hopes for the arrival of someone she lost, despite knowing it's unlikely.
memories.memory_text: I remember Lilka telling me that she keeps hoping someone she lost will arrive, even though she knows it's unlikely.

grounded_facts: Tuvia responds to Lilka's grief by affirming that everyone in the camp has lost someone, including himself.
memories.memory_text: I told Lilka that everyone in the camp has lost someone, because I know that pain too.

grounded_facts: Tuvia removes his wool coat and places it around Lilka to comfort her as she shivers.
memories.memory_text: I saw Lilka shivering, so I took off my wool coat and put it around her to keep her warm.

grounded_facts: Lilka reveals she has been assigned to her first food mission, a dangerous task ordered by Tuvia.
memories.memory_text: I remember Lilka telling me she was going on her first food mission, a dangerous task I had ordered.

grounded_facts: When Tuvia offers to reassign the mission, Lilka insists on going, showing courage despite fear.
memories.memory_text: I saw how scared she was, but when I offered to reassign the mission, she insisted on going, saying she wanted to go.

grounded_facts: Tuvia hands Lilka a revolver for protection before her food mission.
memories.memory_text: I handed Lilka my revolver for protection and asked her if she knew how to use it.

grounded_facts: Arkady suggests that Tuvia has exclusive access to or ownership of the aristocrat, framing her as 'property of the Commander'.
Arkady mockingly references a prior order to keep away from the aristocrat, implying she belongs to Tuvia, which Tuvia denies.
memories.memory_text: I was told 'hands off, property of the Commander'—Arkady said it mockingly, implying the aristocrat belonged to me, but I rejected that idea.

grounded_facts: Tuvia responds to Lazar's challenge by identifying himself and clarifying his origin and purpose.
Tuvia informs Lazar that the danger is coming from those approaching the camp, not from within.
memories.memory_text: I responded to Lazar's challenge by telling him who I am and made clear that the danger is coming from those approaching the camp, not from within.

grounded_facts: Tuvia asks Lazar if there has been any sign of the food mission's return.
Tuvia asks Lazar whether there has been any sign of the returning food mission.
memories.memory_text: I asked Lazar if there had been any sign of the food mission returning.

grounded_facts: After learning the food mission has not returned, Tuvia shows visible concern by looking into the woods anxiously.
memories.memory_text: After hearing the food mission hadn't returned, I looked anxiously into the woods.

grounded_facts: Riva informs Tuvia about multiple cases of pneumonia and emerging signs of scurvy due to lack of vegetables in the camp.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Riva that we have several cases of pneumonia and that scurvy is starting to show because no one's had vegetables in weeks.

grounded_facts: Lazar drags a wounded man back into the camp, initiating a medical response.
memories.memory_text: I saw Lazar drag a wounded man back into camp, which started the rush to respond to his injuries.

grounded_facts: Riva instructs Lazar to bring the wounded man to the infirmary.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Riva tell Lazar to bring the wounded man to the infirmary.

grounded_facts: Riva looks at Tuvia sympathetically, indicating awareness of his concealed romantic interest in Lilka.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Riva looked at me with sympathy, as if she could see through my attempt to hide my feelings for Lilka.

grounded_facts: Tuvia asks Riva about the illness affecting the patients in the infirmary.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia asks Riva about the illness affecting the patients in the infirmary.

grounded_facts: Tuvia resolves to go see Viktor immediately to obtain medicine for typhus after learning the partisans are withholding ampicillin.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tuvia resolves to go see Viktor immediately to obtain medicine for typhus after learning the partisans are withholding ampicillin.

grounded_facts: Tuvia enters the infirmary and inquires about the condition of the sick, prompting discussion about typhus and medicine shortage.
